title: Speedability of computably approximable reals and their approximations
summary: An approximation of a real is a sequence of rational numbers that converges to the real. An approximation is left-c.e. if it is computable and nondecreasing and is d.c.e. if it is computable and has bounded variation. A real is computably approximable if it has some computable approximation, and left-c.e. and d.c.e. reals are defined accordingly. An approximation $\{a_s\}_{s \in ω}$ is speedable if there exists a nondecreasing computable function $f$ such that the approximation $\{a_{f(s)}\}_{s \in ω}$ converges in a certain formal sense faster than $\{a_s\}_{s \in ω}$.
